memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If you pay attention to these laws and are careful to follow them, then the Lord your God will keep his covenant of love with you, as he swore to your ancestors. He will love you and bless you and increase your numbers. He will bless the fruit of your womb, the crops of your land—your grain, new wine and olive oil—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks in the land he swore to your ancestors to give you. - Deut 7:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses describes the blessings that would flow to Israel as they walked faithfully with God — growing families, fruitful crops, thriving flocks. These were the covenant blessings God promised to His people in the land of Canaan, signs of His care woven into their agricultural life. We should read these promises carefully, in their setting. They were part of God's specific covenant with Israel about life in the promised land, not a formula guaranteeing that faithful believers today will always enjoy material wealth.

This is important, because it would be easy to twist these verses into a prosperity message: "Obey God, and He will make you rich and healthy." Scripture never teaches that. Faithful believers throughout the Bible — including Jesus and the apostles — often faced poverty, suffering, and hardship. God's blessing cannot be reduced to a bank balance or good harvests. The prosperity gospel takes promises like these out of their context and turns God into a vending machine for our comfort.

What endures is the unchanging character of God revealed here: He is a generous God who delights to bless His people and cares about every area of their lives. Under the new covenant, our greatest blessings are spiritual — every blessing in the heavenly realms in Christ (Eph 1:3) — and our truest inheritance is God Himself. He still cares for our daily needs as a good Father, but He blesses us most deeply by giving us Christ. Trust His goodness, without turning His grace into a transaction.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I ever tempted to treat God as a means to material blessing?
- What are the deepest blessings God has given me in Christ?
- How can I trust God's goodness without turning it into a transaction?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are generous and good, delighting to care for Your people. Guard me from turning Your grace into a transaction or chasing wealth as though it were the goal. Help me treasure my greatest blessing — Christ Himself. Amen.
